notes: See data/README.md for provenance rules. Every source_url was checked to resolve and to support its definition on 2026-10-16. source_url stays null where no public-domain source has been found yet.

entries.label: DISEASE
entries.plain_definition: Extra fat has built up inside the liver. This is a common finding and is often picked up by chance on a scan.
entries.clinical_context: Graded on imaging as mild, moderate, or severe. Frequently reported alongside liver enzyme results.

entries.label: BIOMARKER
entries.plain_definition: ALT is an enzyme found mostly in the liver. A blood test measures how much of it is in your blood. Higher than usual levels can be a sign the liver is irritated.
entries.clinical_context: Reported in a liver function panel, usually next to AST. Reference ranges vary by lab.

entries.label: BIOMARKER
entries.plain_definition: AST is an enzyme found in the liver and also in muscle. A blood test measures how much is in your blood.
entries.clinical_context: Reported in a liver function panel, usually paired with ALT.

entries.label: BIOMARKER
entries.plain_definition: A blood test that shows your average blood sugar level over roughly the past three months, rather than just at the moment of the test.
entries.clinical_context: Reported as a percentage. Used to monitor blood sugar control over time.

entries.label: DISEASE
entries.plain_definition: Blood pressure that stays higher than the normal range over time.
entries.clinical_context: Recorded as two numbers, for example 140/90. Often tracked across several visits.

entries.label: DISEASE
entries.plain_definition: A hard deposit, like a small stone, that has formed inside the kidney.
entries.clinical_context: Size and location are usually described on imaging reports.

entries.label: DISEASE
entries.plain_definition: One or more hard, stone-like lumps that have formed in the gallbladder.
entries.clinical_context: Commonly seen on abdominal ultrasound. May or may not cause symptoms.

entries.label: DISEASE
entries.plain_definition: The heart looks larger than usual on a scan or X-ray.
entries.clinical_context: Often first noted on a chest X-ray, then looked at more closely with other tests.

entries.label: DISEASE
entries.plain_definition: A part of the lung has not filled with air the way it normally would, so that area looks flattened or closed on a scan.
entries.clinical_context: Often described by location and extent, for example 'basilar' meaning at the bottom of the lung.

entries.label: DISEASE
entries.plain_definition: Extra fluid has collected in the space between the lung and the chest wall.
entries.clinical_context: Usually described as small, moderate, or large, and on which side.
entries.source_citation: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms - 'pleural effusion'

entries.label: SYMPTOM
entries.plain_definition: Swelling caused by extra fluid collecting in body tissue, often in the legs, ankles, or feet.
entries.clinical_context: Sometimes described as 'pitting' if pressing on the skin leaves a dent.

entries.label: SYMPTOM
entries.plain_definition: Difficulty breathing, or the feeling of not being able to get enough air.
entries.clinical_context: Often noted as happening at rest or only with activity, for example 'on exertion'.

entries.label: SYMPTOM
entries.plain_definition: A heartbeat that is faster than the usual resting rate.
entries.clinical_context: Measured in beats per minute. Many everyday things, such as exercise or anxiety, can raise heart rate.

entries.label: SYMPTOM
entries.plain_definition: A heartbeat that is slower than the usual resting rate.
entries.clinical_context: Measured in beats per minute. Can be normal in people who are very physically fit.

entries.label: BIOMARKER
entries.plain_definition: A waste product your muscles make every day. The kidneys normally clear it out of the blood, so a blood test for it gives information about how the kidneys are working.
entries.clinical_context: Reported in a kidney function panel, usually alongside eGFR.

entries.label: BIOMARKER
entries.plain_definition: A number that estimates how well your kidneys are filtering waste out of your blood. It is calculated from a blood test.
entries.clinical_context: Usually calculated from creatinine along with age and other factors.
entries.source_citation: MedlinePlus Medical Tests - 'Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate (eGFR) and GFR Tests'

entries.label: BIOMARKER
entries.plain_definition: One of the types of cholesterol measured in a blood test. It is often called 'bad' cholesterol because higher levels are linked to fatty buildup in blood vessels.
entries.clinical_context: Reported as part of a lipid panel with HDL and triglycerides.

entries.label: BIOMARKER
entries.plain_definition: One of the types of cholesterol measured in a blood test. It is often called 'good' cholesterol.
entries.clinical_context: Reported as part of a lipid panel with LDL and triglycerides.

entries.label: BIOMARKER
entries.plain_definition: A type of fat carried in your blood, measured by a blood test.
entries.clinical_context: Reported as part of a lipid panel. Levels can be affected by what you ate before the test.

entries.label: DISEASE
entries.plain_definition: The fats and cholesterol measured in your blood are outside the usual range.
entries.clinical_context: Based on the combined results of a lipid panel rather than a single number.

entries.label: DISEASE
entries.plain_definition: Having fewer red blood cells, or less hemoglobin in them, than usual. Red blood cells carry oxygen around your body.
entries.clinical_context: Identified from a full blood count. There are many different causes.

entries.label: BIOMARKER
entries.plain_definition: The part of your red blood cells that carries oxygen. A blood test measures how much of it you have.
entries.clinical_context: Reported in a complete blood count (CBC). Normal ranges differ by age and sex.

entries.label: DISEASE
entries.plain_definition: A higher than usual number of white blood cells in your blood. White blood cells are part of how your body fights infection.
entries.clinical_context: Seen on a complete blood count. Has many possible causes.

entries.label: DISEASE
entries.plain_definition: A lower than usual number of platelets in your blood. Platelets are the cell fragments that help your blood clot.
entries.clinical_context: Seen on a complete blood count.

entries.label: DISEASE
entries.plain_definition: Bone density that is lower than usual, but not low enough to be called osteoporosis.
entries.clinical_context: Measured with a bone density scan and reported as a T-score.

entries.label: DISEASE
entries.plain_definition: A condition where bones become thinner and more fragile than usual, which makes them easier to break.
entries.clinical_context: Measured with a bone density scan and reported as a T-score.

entries.label: DISEASE
entries.plain_definition: Everyday wear-and-tear changes in the cushions between the bones of the spine. It is very common as people get older.
entries.clinical_context: Frequently reported on spine imaging, often as an incidental finding.

entries.label: DISEASE
entries.plain_definition: Age-related wear-and-tear changes in the bones and joints of the spine.
entries.clinical_context: Described by the region of the spine involved, for example lumbar (lower back) or cervical (neck).

entries.label: DESCRIPTOR
entries.plain_definition: Not cancerous.
entries.clinical_context: Used to describe growths, lumps, or findings that are not cancer.

entries.label: DESCRIPTOR
entries.plain_definition: A general word for an area of tissue that looks different from the tissue around it. It does not by itself say whether something is serious.
entries.clinical_context: Usually described further by size, location, and appearance.

entries.label: DESCRIPTOR
entries.plain_definition: A small rounded lump of tissue. The word describes the shape and size only, not whether it is harmful.
entries.clinical_context: Reports usually give the size in millimetres and where it is.

entries.label: DISEASE
entries.plain_definition: The thyroid gland is making less thyroid hormone than the body usually needs.
entries.clinical_context: Usually identified from thyroid blood tests including TSH.

entries.label: BIOMARKER
entries.plain_definition: A hormone measured by a blood test that shows how the thyroid gland is being signalled to work.
entries.clinical_context: Usually the first thyroid test ordered, sometimes with T3 and T4.

entries.label: DISEASE
entries.plain_definition: Stomach acid comes back up into the food pipe often enough to cause symptoms such as heartburn.
entries.clinical_context: Often diagnosed from symptoms; sometimes confirmed with endoscopy.

entries.label: DISEASE
entries.plain_definition: Irritation or inflammation of the lining of the stomach.
entries.clinical_context: May be described on an endoscopy report.

entries.label: TEST
entries.plain_definition: The heart's electrical pattern is following its normal path at a normal rate. This is the expected result on a heart tracing.
entries.clinical_context: Reported on an ECG (also written EKG).

entries.label: DISEASE
entries.plain_definition: A heart attack. Blood flow to part of the heart muscle is blocked, so that part of the muscle is damaged.
entries.clinical_context: May be described as recent or previous. Often referenced in past medical history.

entries.label: DISEASE
entries.plain_definition: An area of the body is not getting as much blood flow as it needs.
entries.clinical_context: Described by the organ involved, for example cardiac or cerebral.

entries.label: TEST
entries.plain_definition: Protein is showing up in your urine. Urine does not usually contain much protein.
entries.clinical_context: Found on a urine test, sometimes as part of checking kidney function.

entries.label: TEST
entries.plain_definition: A small amount of a protein called albumin is showing up in your urine, at a level too low to see on a standard urine test.
entries.clinical_context: Measured with a specific urine albumin test.

entries.label: DISEASE
entries.plain_definition: Urine has backed up and made part of the kidney swell.
entries.clinical_context: Usually graded as mild, moderate, or severe on imaging.

entries.label: DISEASE
entries.plain_definition: The liver is larger than usual.
entries.clinical_context: Measured on imaging, often reported in centimetres.

entries.label: DISEASE
entries.plain_definition: The spleen is larger than usual. The spleen is an organ on the left side of your abdomen that helps filter blood.
entries.clinical_context: Measured on imaging, often reported in centimetres.

entries.label: DISEASE
entries.plain_definition: Lymph nodes are larger than usual. Lymph nodes are small glands that are part of your immune system.
entries.clinical_context: Described by location and size on imaging or examination.

entries.label: DESCRIPTOR
entries.plain_definition: Something noticed on a scan or test that was not what the test was looking for.
entries.clinical_context: Very common on imaging reports. Often not related to the reason for the test.

entries.label: DESCRIPTOR
entries.plain_definition: Nothing unusual was seen. In a report, this means the area looked as expected.
entries.clinical_context: A standard phrase in radiology reports. It is a normal result.

entries.label: SYMPTOM
entries.plain_definition: A body temperature that is higher than normal.
entries.clinical_context: Commonly understood term; not flagged for explanation.

entries.label: SYMPTOM
entries.plain_definition: Pain in the head.
entries.clinical_context: Commonly understood term; not flagged for explanation.

entries.label: TEST
entries.plain_definition: A measure of the force of blood pushing against the walls of your blood vessels.
entries.clinical_context: Commonly understood term; not flagged for explanation.

entries.label: SYMPTOM
entries.plain_definition: A sudden forceful release of air from the lungs.
entries.clinical_context: Commonly understood term; not flagged for explanation.

entries.label: SYMPTOM
entries.plain_definition: Feeling sick to your stomach, as if you might vomit.
entries.clinical_context: Commonly understood term; not flagged for explanation.
